newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs higher, boosted by MOF's outright bond buying.
newsitem.headline: JGBs higher, boosted by MOF's outright bond buying.

text.p: The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract was higher by midday on Friday, as it received support from the Finance Ministry's outright bond buying, traders said.
Traders said the firmness in JGBs, however, was somewhat puzzling.

"There are various sell factors such as a rise in money supply and firmness in Tokyo share prices, but JGBs are up regardless. The only reason I can think of is book squaring ahead of the weekend," a trust bank trader said.
The June stood at 123.94 by midday, up from the previous day's close of 123.75. Turnover was 28,562 contracts.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.535 percent as of 0225 GMT, down from the previous day's close of 2.550 percent.
Speculation of a possible further rise in the yen against the dollar may be providing support to JGBs, said an analyst at a major brokerage house.

"One key is whether export firms will sell dollars when it takes another dip below 115 yen. Speculation that the yen may post further gains if such selling emerges, may be providing some support to JGBs," the analyst said.
The dollar was quoted at 116.65/75 yen as of 0230 GMT, up from Thursday's New York close of 115.75/85 yen.
The dollar fell to a fresh low of 114.70 yen in Europe overnight.
Concern that a further rise in the yen versus the dollar may have a negative impact on the economy is also supporting JGBs, a trader for a city bank's securities unit said.

Reported comments by a senior Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) official that Japan may face pressure to raise interest rates led to some selling of JGBs in London overnight, but there was little impact on JGBs overall, traders said.

Jiji news agency quoted Koichi Kato, secretary-general of the ruling LDP, as saying late on Thursday that Japan may face pressure to change its current low interest rate levels as it progresses with financial market deregulation.
The perception is that politicians' talk about interest rates is unlikely to lead to an immediate change in monetary policy, the analyst for a major brokerage house said.
BOJ governor Yasuo Matsushita told a parliamentary committee on Friday that Japan's monetary policy would put emphasis on making the economy recover.
